title: Nasa developing humanoid robots to work alongside astronauts on moon and Mars
key_facts: NASA is developing humanoid robots to assist on Moon and Mars missions with dangerous jobs.
A 16-member Dexterous Robotics Team at Johnson Space Center, Houston, builds the hardware and software.
Possible jobs: repair equipment, move supplies, inspect spacecraft, maintain bases.
Builds on Robonaut 2 (tested on the ISS) and Valkyrie, a 6ft 2in, 300lb, 44-degree-of-freedom humanoid built for the 2013 DARPA challenge.
Tests so far have robotic arms operating spacecraft-style hatches, moving cargo and inspecting equipment.
Goal: robots that take high-level instructions and act on their own because Earth-Mars signals can take many minutes each way.
quote_evidence: Our team is not trying to replace human explorers with robots but instead make human exploration safer and more sustainable.
Tests have already seen robotic arms operate spacecraft-style hatches, move cargo and inspect equipment similar to that used aboard space stations.
why_it_matters_hint: NASA is testing humanoid helpers for future lunar and Mars outposts, with no flight date.
notes: Feature article without a dated event; no mission date given.
